method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **With red flag features, or vomiting without diarrhoea, consider alternative diagnoses.**
claims.source_text: In a child with red flag features or a child with vomiting without diarrhoea, consider alternative diagnoses (see Vomiting)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags:** age under 6 months · bilious vomiting · haematemesis · diarrhoea for more than 10 days · severe abdominal pain · refusal to walk · past GI/surgical history · complex medical history · post organ transplant · immunocompromise · re-presentation or failure to respond to standard therapy.
claims.source_text: Age under 6 months Bilious vomiting Haematemesis Diarrhoea for >10 days Severe abdominal pain Refusal to walk Past gastrointestinal/surgical history eg short gut, Hirschsprung, ileostomy Complex medical history eg renal, cardiac disease Post organ transplant Immunocompromised Representation/failure to respond to standard therapy
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vomiting may precede diarrhoea by 24–48 hours**, but a vomiting child without diarrhoea needs other causes considered.
claims.source_text: Although vomiting may precede diarrhoea in the first 24-48 hours of gastroenteritis, in a vomiting child without diarrhoea, other causes must be considered
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood or mucus in the stool** suggests significant inflammation, as with bacterial infection or inflammatory bowel conditions.
claims.source_text: Blood or mucus in the stool: this suggests significant inflammation that may occur with bacterial infection or inflammatory bowel conditions
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess the degree of dehydration** — it sets the route and rate of rehydration. Weigh the child (bare in infants).
claims.source_text: It is important to assess the degree of dehydration, as this influences route and rate of rehydration … Weight (bare in infants and where practical in young children)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Knowing the cause rarely changes management**, whether viral or bacterial.
claims.source_text: The cause may be viral or bacterial, but knowing the cause rarely changes management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most children with presumed, uncomplicated gastroenteritis need no investigations**, including stool testing.
claims.source_text: For most children with presumed and uncomplicated gastroenteritis, no investigations are required … Most children do not require investigations, including stool testing
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every child on IV fluids: check serum electrolytes and glucose before starting** (typically at cannulation) **and again within 24 hours** if IV therapy continues.
claims.source_text: All children requiring IV fluids should have serum electrolytes and glucose checked before commencing the infusion (typically when the IV is placed) and again within 24 hours if IV therapy is to continue
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BGL, ketones and electrolytes may also be needed** with severe dehydration, profuse or prolonged losses, altered conscious state, hypertonic or prolonged hypotonic fluid intake, complex comorbidities or diuretic use. **Ketotic hypoglycaemia can follow vomiting**, more often in younger children.
claims.source_text: May be required for children with Severe dehydration, profuse or prolonged losses, or altered conscious state Hypertonic fluid administration, eg sports drinks, Polyjoule, NG feeds Prolonged hypotonic fluid administration, eg diluted formula or water-only rehydration … Complex medical or surgical comorbidities or diuretic use … Ketotic hypoglycaemia can be a consequence of vomiting, more commonly in younger children
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stool culture or viral testing is not recommended**, except in unwell children or young infants with bloody diarrhoea, returned travellers with symptoms over 10 days, and immunocompromised patients with fever.
claims.source_text: Stool culture or viral testing is not recommended, except in Unwell children or young infants with bloody diarrhoea Returned travellers with prolonged symptoms (>10 days) Immunocompromised patients with fever
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Many cases are self-limiting** and need only encouragement of fluid intake and monitoring of hydration. **Failure of initial management should prompt a rethink of the diagnosis.**
claims.source_text: Many cases are self-limiting and only require encouragement of fluid intake and monitoring of hydration … Failure of initial management should prompt reconsideration of the diagnosis and management plan
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral rehydration: aim for 10 mL/kg/hr of oral rehydration solution (ORS).**
claims.source_text: Aim for 10 mL/kg/hr of oral rehydration solution (ORS)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mildly dehydrated child refusing ORS:** a short-term flavoured ice block, or apple juice diluted 1:1 with water.
claims.source_text: In mildly dehydrated children who are refusing ORS, short term flavoured ice block or diluted apple juice in 1:1 ratio with water can be offered
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stop any feed fortification.** **Continue breastfeeding, more often**, with extra ORS if appropriate.
claims.source_text: Stop any feed fortification eg extra scoops of formula … If breastfed, continue breast feeding, but more often (or with additional ORS supplementation if appropriate) to maintain hydration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If oral rehydration fails, use rapid or slow NG rehydration**; if NG is not tolerated in a clinically dehydrated child, **move to IV**. IV may be preferred in older children if NG is not tolerated or appropriate.
claims.source_text: If oral rehydration fails with ongoing risk of dehydration, rapid or slow NG rehydration may be appropriate. Failure to tolerate NG should lead to IV rehydration if clinically dehydrated … IV rehydration may be preferred in older children if NG is not tolerated or is not appropriate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ondansetron** may support hydration in children and infants **over 6 months** with persistent nausea or vomiting.
claims.source_text: Ondansetron can be administered to support hydration therapy in children and infants >6 months with persistent nausea or vomiting
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Initial oral ondansetron by weight:** 8–15 kg **2 mg** · 15–30 kg **4 mg** · over 30 kg **8 mg**. **Ongoing dosing is 0.15 mg/kg.**
claims.source_text: Recommended initial ondansetron doses (oral) Weight Dose 8-15 kg 2 mg 15-30 kg 4 mg >30 kg 8 mg Ongoing ondansetron dosing is 0.15 mg/kg
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A response to anti-emetics does not confirm the diagnosis.** Other anti-emetics are not routinely recommended because of side effects.
claims.source_text: Other anti-emetics are not routinely recommended due to side effects … Response to anti-emetics does not confirm diagnosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No anti-spasmodics or anti-diarrhoeals.** Evidence is insufficient to support probiotics.
claims.source_text: Anti-spasmodics and anti-diarrhoeal medications are not recommended … There is currently insufficient evidence to support the use of probiotics to reduce the symptoms of acute gastroenteritis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reserve antibiotics** for enteritis-associated sepsis, specific bacterial pathogens in selected cases (eg *Salmonella* Typhi; non-typhoidal salmonella under 3 months, immunocompromised or septic) or severe *C. difficile* infection.
claims.source_text: Antibiotics should be reserved for treatment of enteritis-associated sepsis or specific bacterial pathogens in selected cases (eg Salmonella Typhi, non-typhoidal salmonella in patients under 3 months, immunocompromised or with sepsis) or with severe Clostridioides difficile infection
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Once rehydrated, restart a normal diet.** Do not routinely restrict lactose; consider it only if stool frequency increases. Diarrhoea may persist.
claims.source_text: Once rehydrated, a normal diet can be recommenced … Temporary lactose restriction should not routinely be advised but if stool frequency increases, it may be considered … Diarrhoea may persist
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** vomiting has reduced and the child is tolerating adequate oral fluids, with nil or mild dehydration.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Vomiting reduced and tolerating adequate oral fluids … Tolerating oral intake and nil/mild dehydration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** if initial rehydration fails or losses are significant, with complex comorbidities, electrolyte abnormalities, an unclear diagnosis or red flags.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Initial rehydration unsuccessful and/or significant ongoing losses Complex comorbidities Electrolyte abnormalities Diagnosis is unclear Red flag features
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** for severe electrolyte disturbance or **shock needing 40 mL/kg of fluid boluses**.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Severe electrolyte disturbance Shock requiring 40 mL/kg in fluid boluses
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
